name: Jalili Syndrome
aliases: Cone-Rod Dystrophy and Amelogenesis Imperfecta Syndrome

ethnicAssociations: Kurdish population (notably described in families of Kurdish descent)

criteria.description: Presence of cone-rod dystrophy characterized by progressive loss of cone and rod photoreceptor function
Amelogenesis imperfecta presenting as hypoplastic enamel defects affecting primary and permanent teeth
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the CNNM4 gene
Electroretinogram (ERG) showing reduced cone and rod responses
Consanguinity or family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both cone-rod dystrophy and amelogenesis imperfecta with identification of CNNM4 gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and clinical ophthalmological and dental evaluation.

laboratory: Dental enamel biopsy showing hypoplastic enamel
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal thinning and photoreceptor loss
Fundus autofluorescence demonstrating areas of retinal pigment epithelium atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CNNM4 gene (autosomal recessive inheritance)
other: Electroretinogram (ERG) with reduced cone and rod responses

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated cone dysfunction without dental abnormalities
Rod-cone dystrophy pattern rather than cone-rod

redFlags: Early-onset progressive vision loss with photophobia
Presence of enamel hypoplasia in both primary and permanent teeth
Family history of consanguinity or similar symptoms
references: Jalili, I., et al. (2002). Cone-rod dystrophy and amelogenesis imperfecta caused by mutations in CNNM4. Nature Genetics.
